findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with repository read access or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permission can retrieve usable AWS credentials.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables (which hold secrets here) are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in plaintext to any principal able to read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would confine access.
The function targets nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unaddressed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL egress boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function or a dependency is compromised.

The assume-role policy trusts lambda.amazonaws.com with no aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount condition, scoping the trust only by service rather than by the specific function or account and creating a weaker-than-necessary trust boundary.
